cards.explanation: The answer is Bethlehem. The LORD says, “I am sending you to Jesse of Bethlehem…” (1 Samuel 16:1) Samuel, the LORD's prophet, gets a town AND a name. That's more direction than I get from my own memory when I walk into a room and forget why.

The reason is that the LORD has picked a king from Jesse's sons. He says, “…for I have selected from his sons a king for Myself.” (1 Samuel 16:1) So the trip isn't random, friends. The LORD already knows what He's doing, and Samuel just has to go and see it.

The answer is that Saul would kill him. Samuel says it straight: “Saul will hear of it and kill me!” (1 Samuel 16:2) Saul is the king the LORD has rejected, and Samuel is afraid of what he'd do. That's a heavy thing to say out loud. You can hear how serious Samuel is, so the LORD gives him a plan right after.

The answer is True. The LORD says, “…and I will show you what you are to do. You are to anoint for Me the one I indicate.” (1 Samuel 16:3) Samuel doesn't have to guess which son. The LORD is going to point him out, and that's a relief for anybody who has ever picked the wrong box at a bakery sale.

The answer is that they ask, “Do you come in peace?” (1 Samuel 16:4) They tremble when they ask it. Samuel answers, “In peace,” and then tells them he has come to sacrifice to the LORD (1 Samuel 16:5). A little trembling in front of a prophet is something I understand, friends, because my mustache does it when the oven timer goes off.

The answer is False. The text says Samuel “…consecrated Jesse and his sons and invited them to the sacrifice.” (1 Samuel 16:5) The sons are invited right along with their father. That's the moment everything is set up for the choosing.

The answer is that Samuel says this one is the LORD's anointed. Samuel sees Eliab and says, “Surely here before the LORD is His anointed.” (1 Samuel 16:6) Samuel sounds sure, friends, REAL sure. And the LORD is about to have a word with him.

The answer is the heart. The LORD says, “For man sees the outward appearance, but the LORD sees the heart.” (1 Samuel 16:7) I've stamped a cookie that looked gorgeous and tasted like nothing, and I've stamped a lopsided one that was the best in the batch. The LORD looks at what's inside every time.
The answer is False. Samuel says, “The LORD has not chosen this one either.” (1 Samuel 16:8) Abinadab walks up, and Abinadab walks away. Jesse still has more sons to bring.

The answer is seven. The text says, “Thus Jesse made seven of his sons pass before Samuel…” Samuel tells him, “The LORD has not chosen any of these.” (1 Samuel 16:10) That's a whole row of sons and not one of them is the one. I'd have needed a bigger room.

The answer is sons. Samuel asks, “Are these all the sons you have?” (1 Samuel 16:11) The LORD has chosen one of Jesse's sons, and seven have passed without being chosen. So Samuel checks if there are any left. Smart question, friends.

The answer is True. Samuel says, “Send for him… For we will not sit down to eat until he arrives.” (1 Samuel 16:11) The meal waits for the youngest. I'd say that's some serious confidence from Samuel.

The answer is that the LORD says, “Rise and anoint him, for he is the one.” (1 Samuel 16:12) After seven sons and a wait, the answer is plain. The LORD tells Samuel which one, just like He said He would. I think the whole room was holding its breath, like when the oven door opens.

The answer is the Spirit of the LORD. The text says, “…the Spirit of the LORD rushed upon David from that day forward.” (1 Samuel 16:13) David is the youngest son, the one who was tending the sheep. Samuel anointed him in the presence of his brothers, and from that day forward the Spirit rushed upon him. The story isn't over, friends.
